Subject: Post-call recap: embeddings & rerank operational constraints and next steps

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap to make sure we’re aligned on the pain, current stack, constraints, and immediate next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Call summary (what you told us)
- Primary use case: personalized recommendation reranking for web + mobile search results (online + periodic offline batch re-ranking).
- Current stack: feature store + embedding generation in-house, vector index hosted in Pinecone (single region), application queries via a microservice layer.
- Index scale: ~120M vectors today; expecting 20–30% growth over next 12 months.
- Vector dim: 1024 (float32), typical payload per vector ~2.5 KB with metadata.
- Traffic patterns: steady peak after content refresh (~30% of queries during 09:00–12:00 PST), and nightly bulk rerank jobs that re-score ~10–15M items.
- Latency targets: p95 <= 60 ms for online rerank endpoint; batch jobs tolerate higher latency but need throughput predictability.
- Cost goal: keep per-1M-query inference cost below your current baseline (your stated target ~ $45 per 1M inferences across generation + scoring).
- Ops pain: unpredictable tail latency on Pinecone during spikes, difficulty reproducing performance locally, and limited visibility into model-level token costs.

What Redwood can address (high level)
- Lower and stabilize p95 latency with model routing (smaller quantized variants for fast paths) and KV prefix caching for repeat queries.
- Reduce cost on batch reranks using optimized batching + GPU-accelerated rerank kernels and offline caching.
- Increase observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency and cold-start diagnostics, and epoch-level regression alerts.

Open technical clarifications we asked to confirm
- Are the nightly batch reranks executed as single large jobs or split across multiple shards (you indicated shards, please confirm typical shard size).
- Do you use Pinecone pods with multiple replicas or a single large instance? (affects our routing plan).
- Any existing hard requirement for exact float32 retrieval vs accepting quantized (8-bit/4-bit) embeddings for rerank stage?

Immediate next steps / asks
1) Please share: a sample query trace (anonymized) and one representative batch job definition (shard size + runtime), plus a small sample of vectors (or a schema/sizes).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your engops + our infra team — proposed slots: Mon 2/23 10:00–11:00am PT or Tue 2/24 2:00–3:00pm PT.
3) We’ll send a short M.A.P. and an initial pricing estimate for online vs batch usage patterns (attached).

Attachments: redwood-embeddings-ops-checklist.pdf (ops checklist we discussed), mutual-action-plan-DataLift-20260220.xlsx (M.A.P.).

If that looks right, I’ll lock in the deep-dive and loop in our infra engineer to scope a small PoC for a single route.

Thanks again,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: embeddings & rerank operational constraints and next steps

Thanks Karthik — good write-up, mostly correct. Couple of clarifications and answers below.

Clarifications / answers:
- Nightly batch reranks: we shard the work into ~50 shards; each shard processes ~200–300k items and runs on our Kubernetes cluster. Total job touches ~12M items currently.
- Pinecone setup: single large instance (we use the standard plan with 2 replicas). We see contention during peak indexing/refresh windows.
- Quantization: we can tolerate 8-bit quantized embeddings for the rerank stage (we still keep float32 for offline analysis). We are NOT ready to move to 4-bit for production at this time.
- Budget sensitivity: our procurement team has asked us to keep any incremental inference spend under ~$30k/mo for the pilot stage.

Helpful artifacts attached to this reply: sample_batch_job.yaml (shard defs, job schedule), anonymized_query_trace.txt (three representative traces).

Can confirm the Mon 2/23 10:00am PT slot works for our engops + Tom (he’s in SF). Please book and share a calendar invite.

Sana Rao
Head of EngOps, DataLift
